title: Policy TTL staleness causing inter-region retry amplification and wrong model rebind
creator: Maya Patel
description: Post-incident follow-up for a late-night capacity/regression event where smart routing policy TTL staleness and a policy rollout race caused many requests to rebind to an incompatible model variant and to trigger cross-region amplified retries. The event increased tail latency, saturated Dedicated pools in eu-west-1, and caused elevated error rates for a subset of enterprise tenants. This ticket captures timeline, root cause, mitigations, and actionable follow-ups.
incident_summary: At ~2025-02-12 02:47 UTC a policy rollout changed routing TTL semantics (shorter TTLs) and a control-plane cache invalidation race left edge proxies with mixed policy versions. A subsequent transient capacity pressure in us-west-2 caused smart-routing to re-route traffic to eu-west-1. Because some proxies still used the old policy mapping, requests were pinned to a model variant that lacked the newer quantization compatibility label, causing the serving runtime to fallback into a slow software path and intermittently fail. The routing decision logic retried across regions with an aggressive backoff that amplified load on eu-west-1, causing Dedicated pools there to burn through burst capacity and degrade. Impacted customers experienced higher latency and increased 5xx rates for ~42 minutes before mitigation completed.
timeline:
2025-02-12 02:47 UTC - Control-plane rollout: changed routing TTL semantics and updated compatibility labels.
2025-02-12 02:49 UTC - First 95th tail latency spike observed in synthetic canaries (not picked up due to monitor thresholds).
2025-02-12 02:51 UTC - Small capacity pressure event in us-west-2 (node reclaim during infra maintenance) triggered reroute policy.
2025-02-12 02:52 UTC - Edge proxies in several regions still held cached old policy mapping (cache invalidation race).
2025-02-12 02:53 UTC - Requests routed to eu-west-1 were directed at a model variant incompatible with quantized runtime path; runtime logged repeated compatibility fallback warnings.
2025-02-12 02:54 UTC - Retry loop: client-level and routing-level retries overlapped and aggressive inter-region backoff amplified traffic toward eu-west-1.
2025-02-12 02:58 UTC - Error budget burn observed; on-call alerted.
2025-02-12 03:03 UTC - Mitigation 1: throttled cross-region reroutes by applying emergency policy to limit retries and reduce per-request reroute concurrency.
2025-02-12 03:10 UTC - Mitigation 2: reverted recent TTL semantics change in control-plane and flushed policy caches centrally.
2025-02-12 03:22 UTC - Traffic and error rates returned to baseline. Post-incident analysis started.
root_causes: Control-plane rollout introduced a TTL semantics change without a coordinated cache invalidation strategy for edge proxies.
A race during policy propagation left a subset of proxies with stale compatibility mappings for model variants.
Routing and client retry interactions were not rate-limited or de-duplicated across layers; overlapping retries amplified load.
Compatibility metadata (quantization-ready flag) was not gated by a strict schema validation; older policy versions could omit it leading to incompatible variant selection.
Synthetic canaries and monitors had thresholds tuned too conservatively and did not detect early tail-latency degradation during rollout.
detection_and_response: The issue was detected by on-call after customer alerts and internal error budget alarms. The first successful mitigation was to apply an emergency routing policy that limited cross-region reroute concurrency and disabled aggressive inter-region retry bursts. We then rolled back the control-plane TTL change and forced a coordinated cache flush. Post-rollback we observed steady decrease in errors. Full incident conference call included runtime, routing, control-plane, and SRE leads.
action_items: ENG-26902: Implement coordinated cache invalidation API in control-plane to atomically update edge policy state (owner: Priya Nair, estimate: 5).
ENG-26903: Add strict schema checks for variant compatibility metadata during policy deploys; block rollout if required fields missing (owner: Liam O'Connor, estimate: 3).

ENG-26904: Introduce routing-level de-duplication and cross-layer retry coordination: add a per-request idempotency key and global in-flight counter to prevent amplification (owner: Daniel Cho, estimate: 8).
ENG-26905: Tune canary thresholds and add a rolling tail-latency monitor that breaks on 95p+ relative delta during policy rollouts (owner: Sofia Rivera, estimate: 2).

ENG-26906: Add automatic fallback gating: disallow routing to variant that lacks explicit 'quantized_compat' flag for customers pinned to runtime-quantized families (owner: Marco Alvarez, estimate: 3).
ENG-26907: Create post-deploy smoke test that simulates cross-region retry storms and validates routing fallback behavior under degraded capacity (owner: Maya Patel, estimate: 4).
ENG-26908: Update runbook for on-call SREs to include emergency throttle knobs for reroutes and a checklist for coordinated cache flush (owner: Priya Nair, estimate: 1).
followups: Schedule cross-team design review for coordinated invalidation API (runtime, control-plane, edge proxies).
Prioritize ENG-26904 for next Major runtime sprint to reduce single-point amplification risk.
Run tabletop incident simulation in Q2 to exercise rollouts with overlapping retries and capacity events.
Audit recent control-plane rollouts in the last 3 months for similar semantic changes and add preflight checks.
Customer outreach: notify affected enterprise customers with summary and remediation steps; Sales/CS to offer incident credits if required.
notes: We observed subtle differences between 'compatibility label present but false' vs 'label absent'. Future policy schema must be explicit (true/false) and default to safe (false). Also separate TTL semantics changes (which affect cache lifetimes) from compatibility mapping changes (which affect routing decisions) so they can be rolled independently.
review_feedback: PM: Add customer comms draft and timeline for outreach (requested by Priya K).
SRE: Emergency throttle knobs should be accessible to on-call via CLI and console; include audit logging for each throttle action.
Runtime: Prefer a defensive runtime path that rejects incompatible variant earlier with clearer telemetry rather than silently falling back to slower path.
